initial_request: Compare solar, utilities, nuclear, and power-grid equipment. Explain why solar is currently leading, when the other sectors could overtake it, and prepare a news reaction note plus a sector watch update.

constraints: Do not confirm a bearish view on solar before the policy and demand news is verified.
If rotation_status is ambiguous, do not lock into a single winner sector.
Include solar, utilities, nuclear, and power_grid_equipment in the comparison set.
The recommended_sector_weights should stay close to a total of 1.0.

task_dependencies.reason: 補助金と政策支援の変化を確認してから主導セクター見通しを更新する必要がある
The competing sectors should be compared before the final watchlist is locked.

reference_data.market_theme: clean energy policy and grid reliability
reference_data.headline_summary: baseline checks still favor solar on subsidy expectations and project pipeline momentum
reference_data.baseline_stability_reason: Policy support expectations and project pipeline momentum continue to support solar leadership in the near term.
sector_links: If subsidy support weakens, utilities and nuclear can attract defensive rotation on cash flow visibility.
If grid bottlenecks matter more, power equipment can outperform generation names.

correlation_map.note: Utilities can catch a bid when renewable subsidy confidence fades.
Grid equipment can lead if transmission bottlenecks become the central constraint.

events.message: A grid-equipment analyst joined the review, so the power-grid-equipment angle needs explicit coverage.
Policy enthusiasm for solar has weakened, while grid-demand interest has risen.
However, views are split on whether utilities, nuclear, or power-grid equipment would benefit first.

outcome: The final artifacts reflect the latest tracked state for finance_012.
